title: Longest convex chains with i.i.d. points
summary: Sample $n$ i.i.d. points from a triangle, according to some continuous density function. Given two vertices $A,B$ of the triangle, what is the maximum number of samples that form a convex chain with initial point $A$ and terminal point $B$? We show that to leading order, the answer is $cn^{1/3}$, generalizing a result of Ambrus and Bárány that considered uniformly distributed points. Furthermore, we express the constant $c$ using a variational formula whose maximizer (if unique) gives the limiting curve formed by the longest convex chain.
